name: schedule_create
description: Create a Host-level scheduled task that delivers a user follow-up to this session, or to a new session, at a future time or on a recurring rule. Use this for reminders and repeated check-ins, not for background work whose result needs a Job handle.

title.description: Short human-readable title shown in schedule lists and used as the created session name for new targets.

prompt.description: The follow-up prompt delivered when the schedule fires. Write it as instructions to the future model turn, not as a status label.

target.description: this_session delivers into the calling session; new_once creates one session on first delivery and reuses it; new creates a fresh session on every delivery.

timing.description: When to fire. kind=after: positive after_seconds. kind=at: absolute RFC 3339 with offset, or {date,time,time_zone}. kind=every: every_seconds >= 60. kind=daily/weekly: local time + IANA time_zone; weekly also needs ISO weekdays. kind=cron: five-field expression + IANA time_zone. kind=rrule: two lines, DTSTART and RRULE.

after_seconds.description: Delay for kind=after; must be positive.

at.description: RFC 3339 instant with an explicit offset.

time.description: HH:mm or HH:mm:ss local wall time for daily/weekly.

time_zone.description: IANA zone such as Asia/Shanghai; required for daily, weekly and cron.

weekdays.description: ISO weekday numbers 1=Monday through 7=Sunday for kind=weekly.

expression.description: Five-field cron expression: minute hour day-of-month month day-of-week.

rrule.description: Two-line RFC 5545 subset: DTSTART and RRULE.

prompt: Host-level scheduled tasks: create, list, view, and edit a persisted rule that delivers a synthetic user follow-up at its due time. `{{tools}}` manage the rule only; the delivered turn does the work. A schedule is not a Job: use `job_*`/`workflow` when you need immediate asynchronous execution, output and cancellation.
